title: I'm Terrified of Using Astra
author: bingewavecinema
selftext: Every time I ask Astra to make a fix, it will create 2+ more bugs elsewhere on stuff it overlooked or wan't ask to modify. I'm also exclusively Claude/Opus 5.5 now. Anyone else have the experience with Astra being more destructive than helpful?

comments.author: Economy_Bedroom3902
comments.body:
I always force AI to write a detailed implimentation plan before it builds anything.  I make "won't do" a list the AI must fill out during the creation of the implimentation plan, and the skill responsible for building implimentation plans has instructions to just focus on the one core requested change.  If I have a bunch of unrelated bugs to fix I will construct a large multi "phase" design/architecture plan which groups them into smaller units, and each phase gets it's own detailed implimentation plan.

I also have an adversarial sub agent who's job it is to review implimentation plans and finished implimentation phases.  It is looking for any recorded changes in the plan or build which were not requested, or are "just a little thing so we can xyz better in the future".

Since I put this system in place I'm much less frustrated with AI overengineering everything or working too hard to "be helpful".  My biggest problem now is my subagent gets annoyed with the feature creep I propose, but I always win in the end.

I like to quote Elon musk to my AI "the best part is no part" and also remind it that a blank slate is easier to grow from than an incorrect "placeholder" feature.
